classification.difficultyReason: Read inverse probabilities from a normal table, justify a midpoint estimate and convert z-scores to contextual design heights.

content.prompt: Australian adult male heights are normally distributed with mean 176 cm and standard deviation 7.5 cm. A doorway is designed so 90% can enter without ducking.

answer.worked: From the table, $P(Z\le1.2)=0.8849$ and $P(Z\le1.3)=0.9032$. Since $0.9032$ is closer to $0.90$, $z\approx1.3$ to 1 d.p.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the minimum doorway height, to nearest cm.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In the Dinaric Alps, male heights have mean 185 cm and standard deviation 7.5 cm. A doorway is needed so 95% can enter without ducking.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Explain why a reasonable estimate for $P(Z<z)=0.95$ is $z=1.65$.

answer.short: $0.95$ lies approximately halfway between $0.9452$ and $0.9554$, so use the midpoint of $1.6$ and $1.7$: $z\approx1.65$.
answer.worked: From the table, $P(Z\le1.6)=0.9452$ and $P(Z\le1.7)=0.9554$. Since $0.95$ lies approximately halfway between these probabilities, a reasonable estimate is the midpoint: $$z\approx\frac{1.6+1.7}{2}=1.65.$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Find the minimum design height, in whole centimetres.

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}x&=\mu+z\sigma\\x&\approx185+1.65(7.5)\\x&=185+12.375\\x&=197.375\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$Round up to give a minimum whole-centimetre design height of $198\text{ cm}$.
